title_ar: الشيخ الددو يترأس فعاليات مهرجان حداء الصحراء للأدب والنشيد في العاصمة نواكشوط.
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Presides over the Ḥudāʾ al-Ṣaḥrāʾ Festival of Literature and Chant in the Capital, Nouakchott
body_ar:
ترأس فضيلة العلامة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء ورئيس جمعية المستقبل مهرجان حداء الصحراء للأدب والنشيد الذي تنظمه جمعية المستقبل للدعوة والثقافة والتعليم في الفترة من 26/05 إلى 28/05/2011 بالمركب الأولمبي بتفرغ زينة مساء كل يوم من أيام المهرجان، إلى جانب محاضرات وندوات صباحية بمقر دار الشباب القديمة.
وقال الشيخ في كلمته خلال الجلسة الافتتاحية لمهرجان حداء الصحراء إن هذا المهرجان جاء محاولة لتحقيق رغبات الشباب ورسالة جمعية المستقبل إلىهم بمختلف أعمارهم، للعناية بهذه الفئة الهامة من شرائح الأمة.
وأضاف فضيلة الشيخ أن السائر علي طريق الله وسنة رسوله محمد صلي الله عليه وسلم يمر بمنزلقات خطيرة ومراحل صعبة، لا بد له من حداء يسر وجدانه ويعين على الاستقامة على الطريق، تماما كما يعين الحداء الإبل على مواصلة السير في الهاجرة ،وهو من فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها.
وقال الشيخ الددو إن الحداء المقصود في المهرجان ليس حداء الصوت، والصحراء ليست صحراء معينة، وإنما الصحراء الحقيقية هي الطريق في الحياة والحداء هو ما يحرك الهمم، ويعين على الاستقامة على الطريق.
وأكد الشيخ أن جمعية المستقبل للدعوة والثقافة والتعليم احتاجت في سيرها علي طريق الله ورسوله إلي "حداء" يؤنسها في تلك الرحلة الميمونة، ولذلك ـ يضيف العلامة الددو حفظه الله ـ كان أول مهرجان لها متعلق بالكلمة الأولي من اسمها وهي الدعوة والثاني بالكلمة الثانية وهي الثقافة، مؤكدا علي أن يكون الثالث عن التعليم وهو الكلمة الأخيرة من اسم الجمعية.
وفي المحور الثاني من الجلسة الأولى من البرنامج الصباحي بدار الشباب قال الشيخ الددو في مداخلته: "إن من لا يحركه الصوت الحسن فاسد المزاج والطبع، وأن ضوابط الشرع في هذه الأمور لا يمكن تجاوزها.."، وذكر أن جمهور أهل العلم على أن النشيد إذا كان مرتبطا بأوتار أو فيه ما يسيء لأعراض المسلمين كان حراما، وما سوى ذلك مباح، وأن الشريعة السمحة جاءت للرقي بطباع البشر وتهذيبها واستطرد الشيخ أمثلة على ذلك، ثم رد الشيخ على الشكوك التي أثيرت حول الأمسية السابقة من أنها كانت فيها أصوات مزامير بقوله: إن ما سمع إنما هو أصوات بشرية طبيعة أجريت عليها معالجة.
وفي ختام الجلسة الثانية من البرنامج الصباحي بدار الشباب – وبعد محاضرات لعدد من الأدباء والشعراء من دول عربية مختلفة إلى جانب أدباء موريتانيين – عقّب الشيخ بكلمة ختامية في هذه الجلسة تناول فيها جانبا من الأدب الحساني مشيدا بإبداع الشعراء الحسانيين حتى في مزجهم بين الأدب الحساني والمعارف الفقهية والأصولية في إشارة منه إلى أن معرفة العلوم الشرعية كانت ضمن الأنماط الأدبية السائدة في المجتمع الموريتاني.
ختام المهرجان:
اختتم الشيخ الددو مهرجان حُداء الصحراء في أمسيته الرابعة في الساعة الواحدة بعد منتصف ليلة السبت، حيث جدد الشيخ الددو شكره في ختام المهرجان لرئيس الجمهورية وحكومته على الجهود التي بذلوها في إنجاح مثل هذه المناشط الهادفة، كما شكر الرسميين والدبلوماسيين الذين حضروا وخصص من بينهم السفيرين الأردني والمصري.
وجدد شكره كذلك للشيوخ والشباب والشابات وتمنى لهم الهداية والتوفيق، كما شكر الضيوف الذين قال إنهم جاءوا من بلاد بعيدة لا يريدون إلا وجه الله وبشر الجمهور بأن المنشد أبو راتب سوف تكون له زيارات في الداخل.
وشكر الشيخ اللجان المنظمة التي قال إنها بلغت عشرين لجنة، كما شكر رجال الأعمال الذين شاركوا في تمويل هذا المهرجان، رجال الشرطة الذين سهروا على الأمن هذه الأيام، ووعد الجمهور بتكرار مثل هذه المناشط في السنوات القادمة، ثم ختم بالدعاء للقائمين على البلد والمشرفين على هذا النشاط، والقائمين على جمعية المستقبل والمنشدين والشعراء وسائر الحضور والمسلمين عامة.
body_en:
His Eminence the erudite Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars and president of the Future Association, presided over the Ḥudāʾ al-Ṣaḥrāʾ Festival of Literature and Chant, organised by the Future Association for Calling to Islam, Culture and Education in the period from 26/05 to 28/05/2011 at the Olympic Complex in Tevragh Zeina, on each evening of the festival, alongside morning lectures and panels at the premises of the old Youth House.

In his address during the opening session of the Ḥudāʾ al-Ṣaḥrāʾ Festival, the Sheikh said that this festival came as an attempt to meet the wishes of young people, and as the Future Association's message to them, at their various ages, in caring for this important segment among the strata of the community.

His eminence the Sheikh added that whoever travels the path of God and the sunnah of His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, passes through dangerous slippages and difficult stages, and must have a driving-song (ḥudāʾ) to gladden his heart and to help him hold to the straight road — exactly as the driving-song helps camels to keep marching in the noonday heat; and it is part of the natural disposition (fiṭrah) upon which God created people.

Sheikh al-Dedew said that the ḥudāʾ meant in the festival is not the ḥudāʾ of the voice, and the desert is not a particular desert; rather the real desert is the road of life, and the ḥudāʾ is whatever stirs resolve and helps one hold to the straight road.

The Sheikh affirmed that the Future Association for Calling to Islam, Culture and Education had needed, in its travelling on the path of God and His Messenger, a "ḥudāʾ" to keep it company on that blessed journey; and for that reason — the erudite al-Dedew, may God preserve him, adds — its first festival was connected with the first word of its name, which is calling to Islam, and the second with the second word, which is culture; and he affirmed that the third would be about education, which is the last word in the association's name.

In the second axis of the first session of the morning programme at the Youth House, Sheikh al-Dedew said in his intervention: "Whoever is not moved by a beautiful voice is corrupt in temperament and in nature, and the controls the revealed law sets in these matters cannot be overstepped." He mentioned that the majority of the people of knowledge hold that chant, if it is joined to stringed instruments or contains what impugns the honour of Muslims, is forbidden (ḥarām), and that what is other than that is permissible (mubāḥ); and that the accommodating revealed law came to raise and to refine human natures. The Sheikh went on to give examples of this. Then the Sheikh answered the doubts that had been raised about the previous evening — that there had been the sounds of wind instruments in it — by saying that what had been heard was only natural human voices to which processing had been applied.

At the close of the second session of the morning programme at the Youth House — and after lectures by a number of writers and poets from various Arab countries, alongside Mauritanian writers — the Sheikh followed with a closing word in this session, in which he treated an aspect of Hassaniya literature, acclaiming the creativity of the Hassaniya poets, even in their blending of Hassaniya literature with the knowledge of jurisprudence and of legal theory (uṣūl al-fiqh) — in an indication from him that knowledge of the revealed sciences was among the literary patterns prevailing in Mauritanian society.

## Close of the festival

Sheikh al-Dedew closed the Ḥudāʾ al-Ṣaḥrāʾ Festival on its fourth evening at one o'clock after midnight on the night of Saturday. At the close of the festival Sheikh al-Dedew renewed his thanks to the President of the Republic and his government for the efforts they had made in bringing such purposeful activities to success. He also thanked the officials and diplomats who attended, singling out among them the Jordanian and the Egyptian ambassadors.

He likewise renewed his thanks to the sheikhs and to the young men and young women, and wished them guidance and success. He also thanked the guests, who he said had come from distant lands seeking nothing but the face of God, and gave the audience the good news that the chanter Abu Ratib would be making visits in the interior of the country.

The Sheikh thanked the organising committees, which he said had reached twenty in number. He also thanked the businessmen who took part in financing this festival, and the police who kept watch over security during these days; and he promised the audience a repetition of such activities in the coming years. He then closed with a supplication for those responsible for the country and those supervising this activity, for those running the Future Association, for the chanters and the poets and all those present, and for the Muslims generally.

flags.arabic: وذكر أن جمهور أهل العلم على أن النشيد إذا كان مرتبطا بأوتار أو فيه ما يسيء لأعراض المسلمين كان حراما، وما سوى ذلك مباح
flags.context: the Sheikh's intervention in the morning session on the ruling on chant
options: keep it as a reported majority position, as the Arabic does
present it as the Sheikh's own ruling
flags.note: CRITICAL. The Arabic says 'the majority of the people of knowledge hold' — the Sheikh is reporting a position, and the record never says in so many words that he adopts it, although the context strongly implies it. Style guide section 1 forbids collapsing a reported position into his own. The two ruling terms are rendered by the fixed mapping of section 3: حرام as 'forbidden (ḥarām)', مباح as 'permissible (mubāḥ)'. This is the only legal ruling anywhere in this record and it reaches the reader through a news desk's paraphrase of a spoken intervention, which is the worst possible chain of custody for a ruling on a contested question. It must not be cited as a fatwa of the Sheikh's.

flags.context: the festival's name and the governing image of the Sheikh's address
flags.note: Dialect and register both matter here: ḥudāʾ is the chant sung to keep camels moving, and the whole address turns on reading it as whatever keeps a traveller going on the road of life. The transliteration is retained throughout and the festival's name is not translated, since the Sheikh himself glosses the name in the body.

flags.context: النشيد إذا كان مرتبطا بأوتار ... أصوات مزامير
flags.note: Both are the classical instrument categories that carry the legal weight in this discussion, and the ruling reported above turns on the first of them. Rendered by category rather than by a particular instrument, since naming one instrument would narrow a ruling the Arabic states broadly.

flags.arabic: إن من لا يحركه الصوت الحسن فاسد المزاج والطبع
flags.context: the Sheikh's intervention at the Youth House
options: translate faithfully and hold for editorial decision
flags.note: Style guide section 12, at the lower end. In Arabic this is a recognisable topos in the literature on listening to song, and it reads as rhetoric; in English, in a news report, it reads as a clinical judgement passed on a class of persons. Translated exactly and neither softened nor strengthened. Flagged so that the decision is a conscious one.

options: preserve as served in body_ar, normalise silently in body_en only
flags.note: Source defects, style guide section 11. The record repeatedly writes alif maqṣūra for yāʾ and the reverse — إلىهم for إليهم, علي for على, صلي for صلى, الأولي for الأولى, إلي for إلى. This is a keyboard/encoding artifact of the CMS, not the writer's usage, and it is corpus-wide rather than particular to this record; it should be cleaned globally and not per record. body_ar preserves every instance exactly as served.

translator_notes: This is a news report written by the site's news desk, not a text by the Sheikh. Everything attributed to him arrives at second hand and in summary, even where the report uses quotation marks. The site must render it as reportage.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the event took place or when the report was written.
The report dates the festival itself to 26-28 May 2011, which the CMS timestamp happens to fall within. That is coincidence and not corroboration; the in-body dates are the evidence.
Style guide section 13 lists fiṭrah as a pending glossary addition. It is rendered 'natural disposition' here with the Arabic bracketed, and the choice is left open for the glossary decision.

'الأمة' is rendered 'the community' per house usage, not 'the nation'. 'أهل العلم' is rendered 'the people of knowledge', the Arabic idiom, rather than 'scholars', so that the reported consensus keeps the shape the source gives it.

Marked critical_for_display: the record carries a legal ruling on a contested question inside a festival report, and a reader landing on this page will take the paraphrased ruling for a fatwa. The site should either suppress the ruling sentence or carry a prominent caveat on it.
